chapter: Glaser, the Arcadia and bands of 1939-41
title: Glaser puts him in the Arcadia
summary: Glaser's ten-piece stayed nine months at the Arcadia, and Roy had to pay for Don Redman's arrangements.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Then I went down to just dig Glaser and to see what he was gonna do. I think the first thing I did was... I think I got ten pieces together. He booked me in... We might have worked some other place before, but it was a...
That's my friend up there, the bluejay. There's two of them fellows that hang out. They're mean, man. They run everybody. All kinds of birds around here.

But anyhow, we went in there [ARCADIA BALLROOM] for two weeks, and we stayed nine months. Not on account of him. Now, he claims that, well, he got the job, which could be true; you know, he had the guy (?). But he didn't keep me in there on account of that. It's because I learned what the... See, when I first went in there, it was sad, because I had all these arrangements, and people had given me... My brother was writing. And he added Don Redman, because he had Don Redman under contract, so Don was getting like a hundred dollars off me, you know. And he had some other White cat, I forget his name, who was writing arrangements, and he was getting a hundred. So you know, every time I'd
get a chance to make a little bread, I had to pay it out for something, you know.
